description: Replace a naive MAX(id)-per-key dedup that silently assumes higher id means more recent with a ROW_NUMBER() dedup keyed on the actual timestamp
prompts: dedupe.sql is supposed to return exactly one row per email from the contacts table - the MOST RECENTLY UPDATED one (by updated_at, not by id - a row can be updated long after it was inserted, so a higher id does NOT mean a more recent update). Rewrite it using ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY email ORDER BY updated_at DESC, id DESC) in a CTE, keeping only rn = 1. Ties on the exact same updated_at break by the higher id (the more recently inserted of the two). Return columns (id, email, name, updated_at) ordered by email.

setup_files.dedupe.sql:
-- BUG: assumes the highest id per email is the most recently updated row,
-- but a row can be updated long after it was inserted.
SELECT id, email, name, updated_at
FROM contacts
WHERE id IN (SELECT MAX(id) FROM contacts GROUP BY email)
ORDER BY email;

reference_solution.dedupe.sql:
WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT
    id, email, name, updated_at,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY email ORDER BY updated_at DESC, id DESC) AS rn
  FROM contacts
)
SELECT id, email, name, updated_at
FROM ranked
WHERE rn = 1
ORDER BY email;

FROM contacts
WHERE id IN (SELECT MAX(id) FROM contacts GROUP BY email)
ORDER BY email;

test_setup_files.check_dedupe.py:
import sqlite3
from pathlib import Path

sql = Path("dedupe.sql").read_text(encoding="utf-8")

con = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
con.executescript("""
CREATE TABLE contacts (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  email TEXT NOT NULL,
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  updated_at TEXT NOT NULL
);
INSERT INTO contacts VALUES
  (1, 'ada@example.com', 'Ada (old)', '2026-01-01'),
  (2, 'grace@example.com', 'Grace', '2026-03-01'),
  (3, 'ada@example.com', 'Ada (newer name, lower id would be wrong)', '2026-05-01');
""")

cur = con.execute(sql)
cols = [d[0] for d in cur.description]
rows = cur.fetchall()

assert cols == ["id", "email", "name", "updated_at"], f"column names/order changed: {cols}"

expected = [
    (3, "ada@example.com", "Ada (newer name, lower id would be wrong)", "2026-05-01"),
    (2, "grace@example.com", "Grace", "2026-03-01"),
]
assert rows == expected, f"expected: {expected}\ngot: {rows}"

print("PASS dedupe.sql behavior checks")
